claims.reason: The two proofs repeat the same argument under the same hypotheses. Both take the lower half of abs_le applied to hV.2.1 on the endpoints, and both bound dist (V γ0) (V γ1) ≤ 2η by the triangle inequality through z. Both turn that into dist (γ 0) (γ 1) ≤ (2η+ε)r with div_le_iff₀. Both use hγ t 0 to get dist (γ t) (γ 0) ≤ dist (γ 0) (γ 1), then the triangle inequality through p. The only difference is the final bound: radius gives (ρ+2η+ε)r, and within gives S·r. Within is therefore the radius lemma followed by mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hroom hr.le. The radius lemma needs no extra hypotheses beyond the within ones. The `omit` shows it only needs MetricSpace X. PointedLocalGeodesic.lean already has the needed definitions (IsPointedApproximation, IsGeodesic, Time) because within uses them. Its imports are PointedGeodesicWithin and PointedRadialDistance, so moving the lemma there creates no cycle. MetricLocalMidpointVolume imports PointedLocalGeodesic, and MetricSetMidpointVolume imports MetricLocalMidpointVolume, so both downstream uses (MetricLocalMidpointVolume line 84 and MetricSetMidpointVolume line 54) keep working. The repeated reasoning is a real multi-step geodesic-confinement argument of about 15 lines, not a short calculation. Keeping one copy removes a duplicate that must be maintained in step. This is untested: I did not compile the rewrite.
claims.shared_lemma: theorem pointed_local_geodesic_radius {n : ℕ} {p : X} {r S ρ η ε : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hρS : ρ ≤ S) {V : X → Euclidean n} (hV : IsPointedApproximation p 0 r S ε V) {γ : C(Time,X)} (hg : IsGeodesic γ) (h0 : dist (γ 0) p ≤ ρ*r) (h1 : dist (γ 1) p ≤ ρ*r) {z : Euclidean n} (hz0 : V (γ 0) ∈ closedBall z η) (hz1 : V (γ 1) ∈ closedBall z η) (t : Time) : dist (γ t) p ≤ (ρ+2*η+ε)*r. It is declared in PointedLocalGeodesic.lean with [MetricSpace X] and no `omit`. The proof is unchanged: endpoint image distance ≤ 2η by the triangle inequality, then dist (γ 0) (γ 1) ≤ (2η+ε)r via hV.2.1, then dist (γ t) (γ 0) ≤ dist (γ 0) (γ 1) via the geodesic identity, then the triangle inequality through p.
